structured_conclusion.macro_trend: Vol/Credit Relief Extends Below MOVE-70 Even As Plumbing Confirms Tightening
structured_conclusion.likely_rotation: Credit, Korea (EWY/Hynix/Samsung), vol-sensitive names lead; SOXX and duration lag as long yields rise and plumbing tightens

bias: Fresh H.4.1 data confirms the plumbing actually tightened overnight — TGA rebuilt +$56.6B, reserves fell to $2.944T, and RRP slid to a near-fully-exhausted $0.45B — even as risk assets kept rallying (MOVE broke below 70, credit proxies broadly higher, EWY +1.4%, KOSPI +2.4%). Long-end yields also rose (10Y +0.67%, 30Y +0.82%), so this reads as a market still pricing disinflation and credit calm even as balance-sheet mechanics turn less supportive. Today's retail sales print is the next real test of whether the risk-on tape or the tightening plumbing wins out.

counterargs.thesis: Risk-on relief continues (vol below 70, credit firm, Korea/semis strong) vs. plumbing turning tighter (TGA rebuild, reserves down, RRP near-exhausted) and rising long-end yields
supporting: MOVE -3.97% to 69.23, breaking below 70 for the first time this cycle

against: H.4.1 confirms TGA rebuilt +$56.6B to $963.95B — reserves draining

US10Y (4.680%) and US30Y (5.262%) both rose today — long end still restrictive and moving the wrong way

counterargs.read: Today is a split tape: the plumbing genuinely tightened (TGA rebuild, reserve drawdown, RRP near zero) while risk assets shrugged it off and continued higher (vol below 70, credit firm, Korea and semis rallying). That combination — tightening liquidity mechanics alongside rising long yields but still-calm vol and credit — is unusual and worth watching closely. If retail sales comes in hot today, the tightening plumbing and rising yields would have a much more direct read-through than currently priced.
